newsitem.title: USA: U.S. weekly rice cash market summary - USDA.
newsitem.headline: U.S. weekly rice cash market summary - USDA.

text.p: In the South, rice prices were steady, USDA said in its weekly rice report.

Long grain milled rice was selling mostly at $20.50 per cwt.; Medium grain traded mostly at $18.50-$19.00; Second heads were steady and Brewers remain in very tight supply with few quotes at $14.50-$15.50.
Rice by-products were lower, bran was $8.00-$15.00 lower, millfeed was steady to $8.00 lower.
In California, rice prices were steady to $1.50 lower, with Medium grain selling mostly at $18.00-$19.00. Rice bran was $5.00-$12.00 higher.

California rice ship loadings for the week ending February 8 at the port of Stockton: The Ammon Ace loaded 8,900 tonnes of U.S. No. 1 medium grain milled bagged rice and 1,100 tonnes of U.S. No. 1 bagged second heads destined for Japan.
At the port of Sacramento The Tinker Bell loaded 9,072 tonnes of U.S. No. 1 medium grain milled bagged rice and 24,438 tonnes of second heads destined for Japan.
Inspections of California rice for export for the week ending February 8, 445,089 cwt of rice inspected. The yearly total since October 1, 1996 was 6,242,687 cwt compared to 5,548,093 cwt a year ago.
